answer: Each identity registers one pearl oyster bed on a basalt reef plot, stakes 75 credits, and files a spat count. An auditor checks the stake's umber tag against its key and recounts spat against the public bed map; a mismatch over 5% burns the bond. The first bed pays 27, the kth pays 27+5(k-1), so the 1,000th pays 5,022; 1,000 fake beds cost 2,524,500 plus 75,000 locked, no bulk discount. An honest agent pays 27 once and recovers 75 after an epoch. A rented-bed ring fails because a rented count bears the seller key or repeats a registered plot, and the recount exposes both.
